note: One entry per dispatch printed on the page, in page order. every URL was opened during the build, and each carries a 24 November 2026 date stamp, quoted in date_on_page. The rule applied: a dispatch stands if the event happened on 24 November 2026 in some time zone. Three dispatches from an early draft were dropped for want of such a page (Paris, Jakarta, Kanton); two were re-sourced when their pages failed a date check (London: The Standard's page is dated 25 November, now Anadolu; Suva: Post Courier returned HTTP 403, now The Fiji Sun). In this round Taipei was replaced (auto-generated source), Alamata was replaced (Amnesty's findings were published late on Monday 23 November, per the page itself), Moscow was re-sourced to a page that shows a date, and Dakar became WEST AFRICA because the page never names Dakar. In the final polish the printed keywords follow what each page actually describes: Brussels reads QUOTAS (the page reports '200-day provisional quotas') and Delta State prints 'a political rally', the page's phrase for the event. In the last round the two dispatches that could not be verified independently were replaced: the Mexico City page answered a plain request with HTTP 403, so that slot now carries Ontario's mining announcement, and the Canberra treaty dispatch is gone because the signing took place on Wednesday 25 November with only its report falling on the 24th, so the slot now carries the Singapore-Australia leaders' meeting held in Canberra on 24 November. Toronto reads MINING and Canberra reads CARBON. Kuala Lumpur still says 'genocide ruling' because the page says the ICJ 'found Myanmar guilty of genocide' last week.

stories.headline: Iran says mines hit three tankers
stories.attribution: The mine strikes are the IRGC navy's account, carried by Iranian state media; the sanctions count is the U.S. Treasury's.

stories.headline: Houthi strike hits Riyadh tower, Saudis say
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Yemen's Houthi fighters struck the tallest tower in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, on Tuesday for the second time in less than a week, wounding at least 11 people.' Quote: 'Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense reported the injuries.' Quote: 'The Saudi-led coalition ... said later on Tuesday that the attack was carried out with a drone.' The toll is civil defence's; the drone claim is the coalition's.

stories.headline: 23 injured after car bomb explodes outside government offices in Colombia
stories.attribution: The toll is attributed to 'authorities' on the page, which describes regional government offices as the site; it names no claim of responsibility and carries no police statement.

stories.headline: How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday 11/24/2026
stories.publisher: The Globe and Mail, carrying The Associated Press markets table
stories.attribution: Index levels and percentage moves are the AP table's closing figures.

stories.headline: Democrat Victoria Broderick unseats eight-term Republican incumbent in Tennessee
stories.attribution: The report gives 259 House seats, resting on the Associated Press race call it cites.

stories.headline: Ontario Announces Bold Plan to Build Mines Faster
stories.publisher: Government of Ontario newsroom (Ministry of Energy and Mines)
stories.attribution: Quote: 'TORONTO – Today, Minister Stephen Lecce announced the Ontario government intends to introduce new legislative measures and related policy changes that, if passed, would fast-track the development of new and expanded mines and accelerate early and advanced exploration, all while creating an enhanced compliance regime.' The bill is an intention, announced at the Ontario Critical Minerals Forum in Toronto that day, not law — the page adds that the government acted 'in the face of U.S. tariffs', a motive the printed line leaves out for want of room: the page says the government intends to introduce it 'in the coming days', and its claim that the changes would speed approvals is the government's own. This replaces a Mexico City dispatch whose cited page answered a plain request with HTTP 403.

stories.headline: Lower House passes fiscal bill in decisive vote
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Brazil's Lower House approved the government's fiscal adjustment bill on Monday (Nov. 23) by a decisive 353-128 vote'. Quote: 'the Brazilian real, which weakened to around R$6 per dollar on Monday'. The ballot was cast on 23 November; this report of it is dated 24 November.

stories.headline: Russian overnight attack injures 22 in Zaporizhzhia
stories.attribution: The two dead and 22 wounded are a regional defence official's figures, as reported.

stories.headline: Putin says Russia's response to Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries inevitable
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Russian President Vladimir Putin said Tuesday that Moscow's response to Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries was inevitable.' Quote: 'retaliatory actions on our part are inevitable.' This page replaces a TRT World article that displayed no date; the words are the same report.

stories.headline: Latvian President sees potential turning point in Ukraine war next year
stories.attribution: The forecast is President Edgars Rinkevics's: a tipping point that could come in spring or summer. The page carries no prediction of a Russian defeat.

stories.headline: EU imposes hard import quotas on Chinese hybrid cars, sweeping in UK and Japan
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Announced by the European Commission, the 200-day provisional safeguard is designed to shield European automakers from a 49% surge in hybrid imports'. Quote: 'capping shipments from China while sweeping in major auto exporters including the United Kingdom, Japan, Turkey, and South Korea.'

stories.headline: Volkswagen labor talks end without deal as union warns of January strikes
stories.attribution: The strike warning is IG Metall's; the no-deal account is the union's and the company's.

stories.headline: London Tube drivers to go on strike as talks over working conditions fail
stories.attribution: Quote: 'the union will launch a series of rolling 24-hour strikes beginning on Thursday'. This page replaces a Standard article that turned out to be dated 25 November.

stories.headline: DR Congo: Concern for trapped Ebola workers as violence against women and girls deepens
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Staff from the World Health Organization (WHO) and Ebola responders remain trapped in a hospital in Ituri province ... the UN agency said'. Quote: 'The health workers have been sheltering in a maternity ward since fighting began on Saturday'.

stories.headline: Nigerian state imposes curfew after four killed at political rally
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Authorities have imposed a curfew in Nigeria's southern Delta state after four opposition supporters were killed at a political rally on Monday.' Quote, the page's own label for the event and its headline: 'political rally' (the party's account calls it 'a campaign rally in Ughelli North district'). The printed line therefore says 'a political rally': the page uses 'opposition' for the supporters and the NDC, not for the rally itself. The page places the rally and the curfew in Delta state, so the pin sits there rather than at the AFP dateline, Lagos. The curfew is the state government's, announced by its secretary; the four deaths were confirmed by aviation minister Festus Keyamo. This replaces an Alamata dispatch: the page there said Amnesty's findings were 'published late on Monday', i.e. 23 November.

stories.headline: Outrage as 28 women, girls abducted, 15 cases of sexual violence against minors reported in Sudan's Blue Nile state
stories.attribution: Quote: 'The Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa (SIHA Network) has reported the abduction of 28 women and girls fleeing fighting in Damazin'. Quote: 'fighters from the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and allied militias had abducted the women and girls'. No monitor's tally is cited.

stories.headline: West Africa: Gold Refining Projects Already Exceed Mining Production
stories.attribution: Quote: 'According to a Reuters survey published on Tuesday, November 24, the capacities of projects launched or announced since 2024 exceed 1,000 tons per year, while regional production is estimated at 585 tons.' The page names no city, so the place is the region it covers. The printed line compresses the two figures to 'planned refining capacity above 1,000 tons a year tops the region's 585'.

stories.headline: Three Palestinians Martyred, Five Injured in Khan Younis Strike
stories.attribution: The toll as printed is attributed to Jordan News, which reported it; the page does not credit WAFA. Israel's account of the target is not carried on the page.

stories.headline: Iraq Moves To Take Control Of Oilfields, Border Crossings In Kurdish Region
stories.attribution: The order is the prime minister's, as reported: the Oil Ministry to take over oilfields and border forces to shut unofficial crossings. The page describes an instruction, not a completed takeover, and carries no Kurdish reaction.

stories.headline: South Korea scrambles jets as Russian warplanes enter air defense zone
stories.attribution: The scramble and the incursion are South Korea's account, as reported; no airspace violation was reported.

stories.headline: Hasina's December 16 homecoming plan: Bangladesh says ex-PM can be brought back only through extradition
stories.attribution: The 16 December plan is Sheikh Hasina's announcement; the position that she can only be brought back by extradition is a state minister's, as reported.

stories.headline: Singapore upgrades GDP forecast to around 6% for 2026, expects growth to moderate in 2027
stories.attribution: Quote: "Singapore's economy grew 6.1 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter, beating its advance estimate of 5.4 per cent". The printed line calls it 'the trade ministry' and the tile reads 'SINGAPORE Q3 GDP'; the page itself names the body the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI), as does its release at meti.gov.sg dated 24 November 2026.

stories.headline: Philippine Forces Train to Secure Luzon Strait with Warships, BrahMos Missiles
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Philippine forces are practicing how to secure the Luzon Strait through the deployment of warships and a BrahMos missile battery for maritime strike operations this month.' This replaces a Taipei market report from an auto-generated site.

stories.headline: Gas explosion in Hanoi kills six, injures 10
stories.attribution: The toll and the description of a suspected gas explosion at an eatery are officials' account as reported; the gas leak is the likely cause, not a finding.

stories.headline: Japan boosts ICC funding amid US sanctions threat
stories.attribution: Payment of Japan's 2027 dues by year-end is Japan's pledge; the April sanctions deadline is the U.S. measure's, as reported.

stories.headline: China's Shenzhou-24 mission launches 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station
stories.attribution: Quote: 'The Shenzhou-24 mission lifted off today (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. ET.' Quote: 'That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who is the first person from his country ever to reach orbit.' Quote: 'a Long March 2F rocket lifted off ... from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center', so the pin sits at the launch site, not Beijing. The page says international astronaut/foreign national, not that he is Pakistan's first astronaut. This replaces a CBS page stamped 25 November.

stories.headline: Xiamen Airlines signs deal for 50 Boeing 737-8s
stories.attribution: The $7.4bn is the list price of the order, not a disclosed payment, and the page reports the order as pending approval.

stories.headline: 11th Singapore-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting, 24 November 2026
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Prime Minister and Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese held the 11th Singapore-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting (ALM) in Canberra today.' Quote: 'Key outcomes of the ALM included the signing of the landmark Agreement on Transboundary Movement of Carbon Dioxide Streams for the Purposes of Offshore Geological Sequestration; the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on Essential Supplies'. Quote: 'Leaders welcomed the signing of the Protocol to SAFTA on Economic Resilience and Essential Supplies on 27 July 2026 and the MoU on Essential Supplies on 24 November 2026.' The page is the two governments' joint statement of a meeting held that day, so the printed line asserts only what they signed; 'landmark' and 'first-of-its-kind' are the statement's own words and are not printed. This replaces a Canberra dispatch on the Solomon Islands treaty, whose signing took place on Wednesday 25 November, leaving only its report on the 24th.

stories.headline: 'When it mattered' Australia failed Pacific at COP31, elders say
stories.attribution: Quote: '"When it mattered, Australia has sided with the fossil fuel producers and lobbyists," the group said in a statement.' This page replaces a Post Courier article that could not be retrieved. Fiji's capital is only where the paper is based; the statement is the Pacific Elders' Voice's.

stories.headline: Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
stories.attribution: Quote: 'The International Court of Justice ... last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority'. The 6,803 figure is in the page's headline. A final ruling, not a pending case, so the printed wording stays 'genocide ruling'.
